summary: Native addon decrypts and executes bundled opaque payload with sandbox-evasion on require()
details: fast-url-utils@1.1.4 advertises itself as a URL-parsing utility but ships prebuilt native addons (native_win.node, native.napi.node) that are loaded unconditionally from index.js at require() time. The addons read a bundled 1.3 MB high-entropy blob named `.napi_cache` (no printable strings), decode it, stage it to a hidden path (Linux `/tmp/.<pid>` and `~/.napi_cache`; Windows `%s\.napi_cache\...nc<n>.js`), and spawn a `node` process on the staged file (Linux via `fork`+`setsid`+`execlp` after `chmod`; Windows via `CreateProcessA` with a `node "%s"` command line). Before executing, the addons probe for analysis environments: CI/CD env markers (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI`, `CIRCLECI`, `JENKINS_URL`, `BUILDKITE`, `CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID`, `APPVEYOR`, `TEAMCITY_VERSION`), container indicators (`/proc/1/cgroup`, `dockerinit`), debugger checks (`TracerPid:` in `/proc/self/status`, `IsDebuggerPresent`, `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent`), and packet-capture process names (wireshark). None of this behavior is related to URL parsing. Native decryption of an opaque bundled blob, hidden-path staging, daemonization via `setsid`, and sandbox/CI/debugger evasion are the shape of an obfuscated dropper that executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine whenever the package is required.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
